newsitem.title: PERU: Peru sees int'l reserves above $10 bln in 18 mos.
newsitem.headline: Peru sees int'l reserves above $10 bln in 18 mos.

text.p: President Alberto Fujimori said the government expected Peru's international reserves to rise above $10 billion within 18 months, up from a current total near $8 billion, local radio reported.

"The country now has reserves with a value of $8 billion, and we expect to break the $10 billion barrier within 18 months," Fujimori said at a business lunch in the Philippines, according to a recording of his speech, which Peruvian radio transmitted.

The increase in reserves was expected to come mainly from the government's privatisation programme of state assets and new direct foreign investment in Peru, added Fujimori, who was in the Philippines as part of a trip to Southeast Asia.
Peru's net international reserves fell to $8.397 billion on November 6 from $8.404 billion the week before, according to latest Central Reserve Bank figures.
The bank's foreign exchange position, or total liquidity minus short- and long-term debt obligations, was $1.603 billion on the same day.
Fujimori has already been in Japan on his Asian tour aimed at promoting investment in Peru. He is also set to visit Thailand and Malaysia before returning to Peru on November 22.
